overview: Black plays ...f5 and ...e6 and usually ...Nf6, ...Be7, ...O-O and ...d6, aiming for ...e5 or a Stonewall with ...d5 and ...c6. White fianchettoes with g3 and Bg2, castles and prepares Nc3, d5 or e4. Black's kingside is weakened but he gets control of e4 and dynamic kingside play. The game is double-edged with real winning and losing chances.

white_ideas.idea: g3, Bg2, O-O and Nc3 with a queenside or central expansion (d5, e4)
Exploit the e8-h5 diagonal and e6 weaknesses with Qc2 and Nd4

black_ideas.idea: Control e4 with ...Nf6, then ...Be7, ...O-O and ...d6 aiming for ...e5
Stonewall set-up with ...d5, ...c6 and a knight on e4

typical_structures.structure: Classical Dutch: Black pawns on e6, d6, f5 against White c4/d4 and a g2 bishop
Stonewall with pawns on c6, d5, e6, f5

character.notes: Dutch is double-edged and unbalancing: weakened kingside and e-file for White, Black's attack on the kingside.

structure.notes: Centre undecided, Black decides between ...e5 and Stonewall.

approach.notes: Standard defence with a few main set-ups; played occasionally by Carlsen, Nakamura.

level.notes: Plans and pawn structures need understanding; not very deep theory.
